name: Sapienza University of Rome
summary: Rome's large public university; eight English bachelor's from AI to Classics plus English-taught Medicine, Dentistry and Nursing.

ib.text: A diploma after 12 years of school; the IB Diploma waives the English certificate. Each degree asks for a test score (SAT, CEnT-S or a CISIA test) and a minimum school average.

programmes.name: Applied Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence
programmes.about: Applied computing and artificial intelligence on a base of maths, physics and statistics, with third-year options, economics or law, and an internship.
programmes.overview: You build a general base in programming languages, software design and development, algorithms and computational complexity, and discrete structures, then add technical depth in parallel and distributed software, computer architecture, networks, databases, human-computer interaction, artificial intelligence and information security. Machine learning, deep learning and learning from big data run through the later courses, and an internship and a thesis are part of the path. Graduates can take junior roles building computing solutions on their own, mostly in software companies and IT consulting firms, especially in big data analytics, or continue to a master's in computer science or a related field.
programmes.ib: EU applicants do not use MoveIN: apply through the degree's own call with SAT (over 960) or English TOLC-I (18/50).
programmes.selectionNote: Needs a test score and a school average of at least 75/100 on Sapienza's scale. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Bioinformatics
programmes.about: Biochemistry, genetics, molecular biology, medicinal chemistry and computer science combined, ending with computational biology, machine learning and an internship.
programmes.overview: The degree joins biology and computer science or information engineering. From the first year you take mathematics, physics, statistics and chemistry alongside the structure and function of living systems at molecular and cellular level, then genetics, biochemistry, cell and molecular biology, programming and the design of software systems, with plenty of credits given to lab work. Internships in companies, public bodies and laboratories and study periods at other universities are part of the design. Graduates work as technical staff, researchers or analysts in biomedical research, health services and biotech or pharmaceutical firms, running systems for clinical and bioinformatic data, or continue to specialised study.
programmes.ib: CEnT-S test (any score above zero) for pre-selection.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-selection on CEnT-S and a school average of at least 75/100, then the degree's admission call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Business Sciences
programmes.about: How modern businesses and financial systems work, across economics, management, finance and law, for consulting and management roles.
programmes.overview: The degree builds a multidisciplinary base in business economics, finance, law and mathematics and statistics, so that you can understand how public and private organisations, real and financial markets and their economic, institutional and environmental setting work. Particular attention goes to reading company data critically, understanding decision processes and judging economic and financial performance, including questions of sustainability. Graduates work as junior to mid-level consultants and staff in budgeting, financial planning, auditing, management control, corporate taxation and strategy, in companies, auditing firms, consultancies and public administration.
programmes.ib: SAT 960+ or CEnT-S 18/55 for pre-selection; a strong maths background is expected.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-selection on a test score and a school average of at least 80/100, then the degree's admission call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Economics and Finance
programmes.about: Economic and financial markets, statistics and forecasting, and the effects of public policy; the English path of a degree that also runs three Italian paths.
programmes.overview: The core courses cover economics and applied economics, public finance and economic history, business, mathematics and statistics, and law, so that you can analyse how economic systems and financial markets work with theoretical and empirical tools. Econometrics and statistics build the skills to model economic and financial phenomena and to judge public policy, with attention to growth, development, governance and regulation. Teaching includes seminars, labs and internships, and elective exams let you shape your own path. Graduates work as international economic analysts in international organisations, companies, research centres, public administration and the non-profit sector.
programmes.ib: SAT 960+ or CEnT-S for pre-selection; a strong maths background is expected.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-selection on a test score and a school average of at least 80/100, then the degree's admission call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Classics
programmes.about: Ancient Greek and Latin with archaeology, art history, law, philosophy and science, reading the Greek and Roman world as part of today's heritage.
programmes.overview: Designed for international students who may have little or no formal background in Classics, the course gives intensive training in Greek and Latin, aiming to take you to the point where you can read complex literary texts. Alongside the languages and literatures you study ancient history, classical archaeology and the legacy of the classical world in medieval, modern and contemporary cultures, with cultural, anthropological and reception perspectives. Field trips, museum visits and library workshops make use of the city of Rome. Graduates work in publishing, journalism and cultural heritage, in spreading knowledge of the ancient world and in translating texts, and many continue to further study.
programmes.ib: SAT or English TOLC-E / English Test HUM for pre-selection.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-selection on a test score and a school average of at least 75/100. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Global Humanities
programmes.about: A flexible humanities and social science degree: history, anthropology, literature, media, law, human rights, migration and gender studies, and more.
programmes.overview: The degree combines literary, artistic, socio-anthropological, historical-religious and political-legal perspectives within a global and transcultural view. You study migration, interethnic communication and transcultural mediation in relation to diasporas, with history, art history, the history of religions, anthropology, sociology, global and public health and comparative law. From the third year you gain experience through an internship, with placements arranged with partner institutions. Graduates work as cultural mediators in the social sector, in international cooperation and reception organisations, and in public and private institutions dealing with migration, or continue their studies in Italy or abroad.
programmes.ib: SAT or English Test HUM, plus an English certificate or a school letter that your IB was taught in English; CV and motivation are read.
programmes.selectionNote: A committee reads your grades (average 70/100+), English, CV and motivation; it may interview you. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Molecular Biology, Medicinal Chemistry and Computer Science for Pharmaceutical Applications
programmes.about: Molecular biology, medicinal chemistry and computer science together, aimed at how drugs and other active compounds are discovered and developed.
programmes.overview: You build a base in three areas: molecular biology, medicinal chemistry and computer science. Courses cover molecular biology, biomedicine, genetics, pathology and immunology, medicinal chemistry and pharmaceutical technology, together with programming, algorithms for molecular biology and drug chemistry, and mathematical, physical and statistical methods. The aim is to understand how active compounds are found and how information technology is changing that work. Graduates are prepared for basic and applied research in university and industry labs, biotechnology firms, and scientific publishing and communication, or for further study.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-selection on a test score and a school average of at least 60/100, then the degree's admission call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Sustainable Building Engineering
programmes.about: Civil engineering for sustainable buildings: low energy demand, passive design, recycled materials, longer building life and urban renewal, on the Rieti campus.
programmes.overview: The degree trains building engineers who weigh the economic, social and environmental effects of changing the built territory. Alongside foundation subjects you take core building engineering courses integrated with traditional civil engineering, with environmental engineering subjects giving weight to sustainability, and you learn to survey and analyse existing buildings and to work with low-impact techniques and materials. The aim is to understand the links between management, design, construction and production at different scales of the building sector. Graduates are intermediate-level professionals who contribute to planning, designing and carrying out interventions to build, transform and conserve buildings.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-selection on a test score and a school average of at least 80/100, then the degree's admission call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Nursing (Azienda Ospedaliera Sant'Andrea)
programmes.about: A three-year nursing degree taught in English, with clinical training at Rome's Sant'Andrea hospital.
programmes.overview: The course trains nurses to manage preventive and care interventions for individuals, families and communities, and to look after patients from children to older adults with respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, digestive, neurological, cancer, infectious and orthopaedic problems, as well as perioperative care, safe medication and psychological distress. Theory in basic, clinical and nursing sciences, ethics, law and communication is combined with supervised clinical training at Rome's Sant'Andrea hospital. Graduates are prepared to work as nurses in hospitals and the wider health service, working in teams with other professionals and using the methods of nursing research.
programmes.ib: Admission test set by the degree's official call; not part of the MoveIN pre-selection.
programmes.selectionNote: Places filled by admission test score under the official call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Medicine and Surgery "F"
programmes.about: Sapienza's six-year medical degree taught in English, leading to the degree in Medicine and Surgery.
programmes.overview: Over six years you move from the basic sciences, typically anatomy, physiology, biochemistry and pathology, to clinical medicine, learning to give safe, high-quality care, to make clinical decisions on prevention, diagnosis and treatment, and to base them on evidence while knowing the limits of your competence. The programme follows international standards in medical education and includes a practical-evaluative internship that is required before registration as a physician. Graduates practise in the national health service and in private or affiliated facilities, working in teams with other health professionals, and can continue to specialist training.
programmes.ib: Admission test set by the official call; not part of the MoveIN pre-selection.
programmes.selectionNote: Places filled by admission test score under the official call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics
programmes.about: A six-year dentistry degree taught in English, covering oral and maxillofacial sciences and dental prosthetics.
programmes.overview: Over six years taught in English, you learn to treat diseases of the mouth and teeth and to restore or maintain oral function, starting from the basic medical sciences and moving into clinical dentistry. A large share of the course is professional training: small-group practical activity guided by teachers within the teaching hospital and in the wider area. Dentists diagnose and treat diseases and anomalies of the teeth, mouth, jaws and related tissues and handle prevention and rehabilitation, and they coordinate dental teams that include hygienists, assistants and dental technicians. Graduates can go on to dental specialty schools such as oral surgery and paediatric dentistry.
programmes.ib: Admission test set by the official call; not part of the MoveIN pre-selection.
programmes.selectionNote: Places filled by admission test score under the official call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: Pre-selection is only step one: a pre-accepted applicant still has to take part in the degree's admission call, whose dates are set each year.
You may send at most two pre-selection applications per academic year.
The 2027-28 pre-selection has not opened yet; the 2026-27 round opened on 22 December 2025 and stayed open to EU applicants until 31 July 2026.
